::: {#rem-kolmogorov-vs-entropy}
#### Entropy describes a distribution; Kolmogorov complexity describes a string

Entropy is the expected
[surprisal](https://morrison-lab.github.io/ids/entropy.html#def-surprisal)
of a random variable, so it is a property of a distribution
and says nothing about any one outcome.
Kolmogorov complexity is a property of one string and needs no distribution.
@thm-kolmogorov-entropy says that the two agree on average,
per symbol, for long independent sequences.
For a single string they can disagree:
the string $0101\ldots01$ in @exm-kolmogorov-simple-strings
has as many ones as zeros,
like a typical outcome of fair coin flips, whose entropy is 1 bit per flip,
but its Kolmogorov complexity per digit, $K(x \mid n)/n \le c/n$, tends to 0.

:::
